what: User directive 2026-04-23 on shared-content refactor evaluation: when deciding whether to unify near-duplicate source files (e.g., per-editor rule templates, rules skills, markdown fragments) into a shared body + per-variant overlay, evaluate NEUTRALLY — not lazily choosing "keep separate" to avoid work. Two-step test: (1) If easy to extract a shared source + lightweight per-variant overlay with consistent, predictable rendering → DO IT. (2) If it would be complex, error-prone, or cause inconsistency between variants → KEEP SEPARATE, but add explicit guidance somewhere (a README, header comment block, or doc section) naming the SOURCE-OF-TRUTH file + listing the derived/parallel files, so any teammate updating one knows which peers to sync. The outcome to avoid is silent drift — parallel files that slowly diverge because nobody knew they were meant to stay aligned. Applies beyond rule templates: any "5 variations of the same doc/skill/config" pattern.
why: User corrected my framing of "scope split" as a one-way deferral. Real directive: pick the decision on technical merit (easy overlay = do it; complex = defer) but ALWAYS guard against drift by marking a source-of-truth when separating. This is a process-level preference that applies to many future judgment calls, not just the rule templates. Surfacing it at session start prevents the "pick separation by default to avoid work" anti-pattern.
